title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Confirmatory Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) measuring the effect of template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (and limited automated repair) on deterministic-validator acceptance of LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially crafted intents. The preregistered estimand was the paired difference in per-intent validator acceptance-for-deployment (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). We ran the frozen plan on 150 adversarial intents (planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete_pairs_included = 141) using a single generator (gpt-5-mini) and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Observed complete-pair outcomes: baseline accepted 135/141 (95.74468085%); guarded accepted 141/141 (100.0%); paired difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. We incorporated reviewer clarifications: (1) runtime sampling configuration recorded "temperature": null in the archived model configuration (unset—provider defaults may apply and thus sampling may not be deterministic); (2) provider-call accounting confirmed shared_initial_generation = 150 and repair-stage calls = 6 (hosted_model_call_event_count = 156; completed = 147; failed = 9), which is consistent with shared_initial_candidate semantics and repair-only extra calls; (3) the preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed and therefore no benign-blocking claims are made. Limitations (synthetic tasks, single model and validator, missing benign-control) constrain external claims. Archived execution and analysis artifacts support all numeric claims.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs can translate operator intent to device CLI, reducing manual effort but introducing syntax, topology and semantic risks and new attack surfaces (e.g., prompt injection). Prior work shows that pairing LLM generation with deterministic verification and limited repair reduces some error classes and improves deployability of generated configurations [1]–[3]. Motivated by operational safety concerns, we ask: How effective are template-based input sanitization plus deterministic verifier-gating at preventing adversarially crafted intents from producing configurations that a deterministic validator would accept for deployment? We contribute: (1) a preregistered confirmatory experiment (cand-2026-03) with a formal paired estimand measuring deterministic-validator acceptance-for-deployment; (2) an artifact-backed analysis showing a small, statistically detectable absolute increase in validator-accepted configurations when using sanitization + verifier-gating + limited repair versus an unguarded baseline on synthetic adversarial intents; and (3) targeted clarifications requested during peer review (sampling semantics and execution accounting). We used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics: the same initial sampled candidate was reused for paired Baseline and Guarded conditions, so any paired differences derive from post-generation sanitization, verifier-gating, or the permitted repair stage rather than from differing first-pass model samples.
sections.related_work: Deterministic verification tools (Header Space Analysis, NetPlumber, VeriFlow) provide fast checks of forwarding and configuration invariants and have been proposed as validators for generate–validate pipelines [2],[37]. Experiments in NetOps show LLMs can produce useful drafts but often commit syntax/semantic errors; integrating verifier feedback and repair improves outcomes in prototype tasks [3],[44]. Survey papers and benchmarks emphasize fragmented evaluation practices and call for operationally meaningful metrics beyond token-level or reference-match scores [4],[5]. Security literature documents prompt-injection and indirect prompt attacks, motivating input sanitization and gating defenses in LLM-integrated systems [6]. Tool-augmented LLM orchestration (e.g., Toolformer) illustrates patterns for calling external checks during generation and repair [7]. Our work conducts a preregistered, artifact-backed confirmatory evaluation of a sanitization + verifier-gating architecture under a constrained synthetic adversary model.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The study cand-2026-03 (preregistration SHA-256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373) preregistered the primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where each intent's binary outcome = 1 iff the deterministic validator would accept the generated configuration for deployment. Design and interventions. Confirmatory paired design on N=150 adversarial intents (planned episodes = 300). Conditions: Baseline = single-shot LLM generation (gpt-5-mini); Guarded = template-based input sanitization applied to the intent pre-generation plus deterministic verifier-gating applied post-generation; up to one automated repair call was permitted per run. Generation semantics were implemented as shared_initial_candidate (see Introduction). Execution and instrumentation. Components declared in the archived run: generator = gpt-5-mini; validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; orchestration adapter = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The archived model configuration recorded "temperature": null (unset); an unset temperature does not imply deterministic sampling (temperature=0) because provider-side defaults may apply. Provider-call accounting from the archived reconciliation confirms hosted_model_call_event_count = 156, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 147, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 9, with stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 150 and repair = 6. These counts confirm Guarded reused the shared_initial_candidate in paired comparisons and invoked extra model calls only when repair triggered. Missingness and exclusions. Pairs were excluded only when both paired runs were technical failures per the preregistered missingness_plan. The archived reconciliation documents completed episodes = 282 and failed = 18; complete pairs included in primary analysis = 141. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; this omission is reported and treated as an unperformed preregistered item.
sections.results: Execution summary. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; failed episodes = 18; model_calls_used = 156. Primary confirmatory analysis used the 141 complete pairs. Observed outcomes: baseline_successes = 135/141 = 0.9574468085; guarded_successes = 141/141 = 1.0. Paired contingency: n11 = 135; n10 (guarded=1, baseline=0) = 6; n01 = 0; n00 = 0. Inference and precision. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125. Point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]; the CI half-width ≈ 0.0319 and excludes zero at α = 0.05. Pair mechanism. Archived validator and repair traces show the six discordant n10 pairs correspond to cases where sanitization and/or the permitted automated repair changed the presentation or content seen by the deterministic validator and thereby enabled acceptance where the unguarded baseline failed to produce an accepted candidate. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were used, these paired differences arise from post-generation sanitization/repair and the validator gate rather than from differing first-pass samples. Missingness sensitivity. Conservatively treating both-missing pairs (9 pairs where both runs failed) as failures yields baseline = 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded = 141/150 = 0.9400; discordant counts driving McNemar are unchanged and p = 0.03125. Unperformed preregistered items. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore we do not report an empirical false-positive-blocking rate and caution that claims about blocking behavior on benign inputs cannot be made from this run.
sections.discussion: Interpretation. Under the formal estimand (validator-accepted-for-deployment), the guarded pipeline produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in validator-accepted configurations (≈4.255 percentage points) on the included pairs. The archived traces indicate this improvement stemmed from sanitizer/repair enabling acceptance in a small set of discordant cases rather than from gating that rejected otherwise-accepted unsafe outputs. Operational implications. In this constrained synthetic setting, (1) template-based sanitization plus limited automated repair can recover valid, deployable configurations that an unguarded baseline fails to produce; and (2) deterministic gating remains necessary as a safety boundary but should be co-designed with repair/sanitization to avoid rejecting reparable candidates. Threats to validity. Construct validity: the deterministic validator encodes a limited set of safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants) and omits some protocol-level runtime semantics. External validity: single-model (gpt-5-mini), single validator and synthetic intents limit generalization to production multi-vendor, multi-protocol networks. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced effective N; exclusions followed the preregistered missingness_plan. Security coverage: adversary model was limited to intent mutations of synthetic templates; richer prompt-injection vectors (e.g., multi-source retrieval-augmented pipelines) remain untested. Missing preregistered analyses: absence of the benign-control prevents reporting false-positive-blocking rates. Practical significance. Given the high baseline acceptance rate (ceiling effect), the absolute effect size is small; operators should weigh this marginal improvement against deployment complexity and validate gating/repair behavior on representative benign inputs before production use.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered confirmatory experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank shows that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and limited automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated network configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). The improvement derived from sanitizer/repair enabling acceptance in six discordant cases; it should not be read as a direct measurement of reduced attacker-success without a separate estimand defining attacker-success. Important limitations (synthetic tasks, single model and validator, and an unexecuted benign-control) constrain external claims. Future work should broaden validator coverage, diversify models and vendors, execute the preregistered benign-control and false-positive analyses, and evaluate defenses against richer prompt-injection threat models. Archived execution and analysis artifacts support the numeric claims reported here.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock under the archived master prompt (provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; all literature review, preregistration, study selection, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer-review cycles, manuscript drafting, and revision reported here were performed autonomously after the lock. Declared models/tools and orchestration: primary generator = gpt-5-mini (archive provider field recorded as openai_responses), deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, orchestration adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration: study cand-2026-03 was preregistered prior to observing outcomes (preregistration SHA-256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). Runtime sampling settings: the archived model configuration recorded an unset sampling temperature ("temperature": null), which does not imply deterministic sampling because provider-side defaults may apply. Provider-call accounting and execution accounting referenced in the manuscript are archived with the run artifacts. No human manually edited or corrected the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock. Full run traces, tool-call logs, validator traces, and archived analysis artifacts are available in the submitted evidence bundle for machine verification; the Disclosure intentionally omits per-file manifests and extensive execution-log detail, which remain in the archive.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated here.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
